# Components

What a note can carry. A note is a markdown file, and each block under `ghost:` in its frontmatter is a component attached to it. **New** in the notes list makes a note with nothing attached, **+** attaches a component and the × on its card takes it off again, and what a note does is read off what it has attached.

Components - the parts a note is made of (next/notes.md, "A component"). One registry shaped like `Medium`'s: each entry says what the component is, what it needs and gives, the components it brings with it, the room it takes in a A note is what its components make it: one kind of new note (its words only), and "+" attaches the rest (`attach_menu`). What a note can do, which panel runs it (`workspace_of`) and what it may take next are read off what is attached, never off a list of kinds of note.

Needs and provides are typed names ghost matches ("text", "audio", "reading", "picture", "moments"). A component never names another to work, only what it needs, so a need nobody provides is a sentence on a card.

Slots say how many (`SLOTS`): components naming the same slot are alternatives, and a note has one of them.

The stage is a capability: anything shown on it asks for `forward_plus`, the desktop renderer, so on a phone every component but the text is impossible and "+" offers nothing.

A row's `comes_with` marks a part never attached by itself that brings nothing: its block is kept by whichever of those components the note has (`blocks_of`), and a note carrying its block with none has the first (`attached_of`).

A row's `script` is the path of the script that builds the component's card, loaded when a panel builds it (`NoteCards.make`); by path because this registry is under every card. The script answers `KEY` (its block), `for_note(ctx)`, `capture()` and `apply(block)`; `tests/notes/components_check.gd` holds each to that.

Static and free of autoload names, like `Capabilities`, so a gate can read it under `--script`.

Registry: `Components.REGISTRY` in [src/notes/components.gd](../src/notes/components.gd) (15 components, 2 slots, 4 workspaces).

## Slots

Where a note has room for exactly one. Components that take the same slot are alternatives: **+** grays the second, and says which to detach.

| Slot | What it is | Taken by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clock` | What the show is timed by, and how long it is: a song, a voice reading the text, or a clip. | Song, Voice, Clip |
| `presentation` | What the show is seen in: the Medium and the format it names, a card table, an actor's room, or a clip's own frame. | Medium, Actor, Clip |

## Workspaces

The panels that run a note. Most components are a card on whichever panel is up; a few are an editor of their own and name the workspace that is. Where two attached components name one, a component another brings gives way to the one that brings it.

| Workspace | Named by | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Note** (`note`) | no component: the default | The note's own panel: its words, and a card for each thing attached. |
| **Reading** (`reading`) | Voice | A voice reads the note: the cast, each speaker's delivery and room, the stream. |
| **Table** (`table`) | Table | A show at a table: the episodes agents make from the note's brief, and the voice that reads them. |
| **Masking** (`clip`) | Clip | A clip's editor: its markers, tracks, effects and timeline. |

## Components

By family - the color a component's card, chip and marks are drawn in.

### Text

- **Text** (`text`) - The note's own words: what a voice reads, the brief agents work from, or just a note.
  - gives text
- **Direction** (`direction`) - Where to take what is made next: every agent making the next episode is told it first. The note's own words stay as you wrote them.
  - asks for `agent:writer`; kept in `direction:`
- **Intro & outro** (`bookends`) - Seconds held before the first word and after the last, and how the show opens.
  - needs audio; asks for `forward_plus`; kept in `bookends:`

### Producer

- **Table** (`table`) - Agents plan, build, paint and write a show at a table, one beat at a time, and a voice reads it. The note's words are the brief they all work from.
  - needs text; gives text, picture, moments, episode; brings Voice, Medium; asks for `forward_plus`, `subprocess`, `agent:writer`, `agent:painter`; kept in `table:`

### Voice

- **Voice** (`voice`) - A voice reads the note: a cast of speakers, each with their own delivery and room, in a local neural voice or Ghost Notes' own formant synthesizer (its voices bred in the Lab's fishing game).
  - needs text; gives audio, reading, moments; takes the clock; asks for `stage`, `subprocess`, `python:voice`; kept in `voice:`
- **Voice training** (`voice_training`) - Teaches a voice to speak like someone, from their recordings - files, a folder, or links to videos. The note reads in it, and any Voice card can pick it.
  - needs reading; brings Voice; asks for `subprocess`, `ffmpeg`, `python:voice`, `python:speech`, `python:download`, `python:voice_train`; kept in `voice_training:`

### Sound

- **Song** (`song`) - A song the show is timed by: its beat and its spectrum drive the scenes.
  - gives audio; takes the clock; asks for `stage`; kept in `song:`

### Picture

- **Scenes** (`scenes`) - The visualizer scenes, cut to the sound: picked by the seed, or in the order the note's storyboard writes them (its timeline, beside Play).
  - needs audio; gives picture, moments; asks for `forward_plus`
- **Pictures** (`illustrations`) - The note's pictures: painted by an agent from the image marks in its words, imported from a file, or made by a show's agents for its episode.
  - needs text; gives picture; comes with Medium, Table; asks for `forward_plus`; kept in `illustrations:`
- **Actor** (`actor`) - An actor reads the note in their own room, learned from their own videos - their look, motion, face and voice, every pixel their own.
  - needs reading; gives picture; brings Voice; takes the presentation; asks for `forward_plus`, `subprocess`, `ffmpeg`, `python:face`, `python:speech`, `python:download`, `agent:writer`; kept in `actor:`
- **Clip** (`clip`) - A video from a file or a link, with chroma-key effects over it: markers, tracks and renders.
  - gives picture, audio; takes the clock and the presentation; asks for `forward_plus`, `subprocess`, `ffmpeg`; kept in `clip:`

### Medium

- **Medium** (`medium`) - What the note is shown in - Auto (the seeded show), full frame, a comic, a novel, a notebook, a tablet, a letter or a dispatch desk; a table show at its table or a desk - and that format's settings.
  - needs picture; gives places; brings Scenes; takes the presentation; asks for `forward_plus`; kept in `medium:`

### Look

- **Look** (`look`) - A finish over the whole picture: filters such as grain, noir and a vignette, the tonemapper, and how subtitles appear.
  - needs picture; asks for `forward_plus`; kept in `look:`
- **Masks** (`masks`) - Chroma-key effects over a clip: markers, tracks and renders.
  - needs picture; brings Clip; asks for `forward_plus`, `subprocess`, `ffmpeg`

### Publish

- **YouTube** (`youtube`) - Uploads the exported video to your YouTube channel: its title, thumbnail, privacy and playlist.
  - needs picture, audio; asks for `movie_export`, `subprocess`, `ffmpeg`; kept in `youtube:`

## Capabilities

What a component may ask of the platform. Each is possible somewhere or not at all, and **+** leaves out what is impossible here and grays what is not ready yet, with the reason; the same table is checked wherever a program is started. On a phone, a note is its text and nothing else.

| Capability | What it is | Possible on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subprocess` | starting programs | the desktop |
| `ffmpeg` | FFmpeg | the desktop |
| `python:voice` | the voice environment | the desktop |
| `python:download` | the download environment | the desktop |
| `python:capture` | the page-capture environment | the desktop |
| `python:face` | the body and face-tracking environment | the desktop |
| `python:speech` | the speech-recognition environment | the desktop |
| `python:voice_train` | the voice-training environment | the desktop |
| `tex` | TeX | the desktop |
| `python:math` | the math environment | the desktop |
| `agent:writer` | an AI writer | the desktop |
| `agent:painter` | an AI painter | the desktop |
| `movie_export` | rendering a video | the desktop |
| `checkout` | running from the repository | a checkout of the repository |
| `forward_plus` | the desktop renderer | the desktop |
| `stage` | the show (a stage that plays) | the desktop |
| `mic` | a microphone | the desktop |

Source: `Capabilities.TABLE` in [src/platform/capabilities.gd](../src/platform/capabilities.gd)
